name: You're taller in the morning

hook_variants.template: You're taller right now than you'll be tonight. By almost 2 centimeters.
When are you at your tallest: morning or night?
You lose up to 2 cm of height every single day.

sections.text: Your spine is 33 stacked bones with soft discs in between. Gravity squeezes them all day.
By evening, the discs lose fluid and you shrink by about 1 to 2 centimeters.
sections.subtitle: lost by the end of the day

sections.text: At night, lying flat removes the squeeze. The discs rehydrate and puff back up.
sections.title: the cycle

sections.text: Astronauts get the reverse: without gravity, their spines stretch up to 3 percent taller.
sections.title: space version

sections.text: Static? No — you're literally changing height in real time.
sections.title: Daily height swing
sections.label: ~1-2 cm

sections.text: Follow for more facts about the machine you live in.

facts.claim: Intervertebral discs rehydrate overnight, making people taller in the morning and shorter by evening
The human spine consists of 33 vertebrae with discs between them
Astronauts can become several centimeters taller in microgravity due to spinal disc expansion
facts.source_name: Wikipedia — Spaceflight effects on the human body

titles: Why you shrink 2 cm every day
